dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical conjunction of two propositions.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Nests the five asserted components: probability-measure status, measurability, positivity of the scale, the universal nonnegative-parameter bound, and existence of a negative-parameter failure.

dependency_coverage.name: Exists
dependency_coverage.meaning: Existential quantification over a type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Requires a real parameter lam witnessing the negative-parameter failure of the displayed integral bound.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Heterogeneous multiplication supplied by an HMul instance; here all operands and results are real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Forms the real products lam * |X x| and K3 * lam in the two exponential expressions.

dependency_coverage.name: InnerProductSpace.toNormedSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: Extracts the normed-space structure associated with an inner-product-space structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supplies the real normed-space instance needed to interpret the real-valued Bochner integral; it adds no mathematical condition to the proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: Inv.inv
dependency_coverage.meaning: Multiplicative inversion from an Inv instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Forms K3^{-1}, the magnitude limit for both the universal nonnegative parameter and the existential negative parameter.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: The less-than-or-equal relation supplied by an LE instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Expresses 0 <= lam, lam <= K3^{-1}, the exponential-integral upper bound, and |lam| <= K3^{-1} for the negative witness.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.meaning: The strict less-than relation supplied by an LT instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Expresses both 0 < K3 and the requirement lam < 0 on the existential witness.

dependency_coverage.name: Measurable
dependency_coverage.meaning: A function is measurable when preimages of measurable sets are measurable.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Asserts that the fixed constant-zero function X from the Borel real line to itself is measurable.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure
dependency_coverage.meaning: A predicate asserting that a measure is a probability measure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Asserts probability-measure status for the fixed measure mu, which is the Dirac measure at zero.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Measure
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of measures on a type equipped with a measurable-space structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Provides the type of the fixed Borel measure mu on the real line.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructs the Dirac point-mass measure concentrated at a specified point.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Defines mu to be the point mass at the real number zero.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.integral
dependency_coverage.meaning: The measure-theoretic Bochner integral of a function with values in a real normed vector space.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Forms the real integral of exp(lam * |X x|) with respect to mu in both the universal bound and its existential failure.

dependency_coverage.name: NormedAddCommGroup.toSeminormedAddCommGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: Forgets part of a normed additive commutative group structure to obtain its seminormed additive commutative group structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supports the structural instances used by the real-valued integral and imposes no additional proposition-level restriction.

dependency_coverage.name: Not
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical negation, defined as implication to false.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Negates the integral upper bound at the existential negative parameter, so that parameter must be an actual counterexample to the inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat

dependency_coverage.name: One.toOfNat1

dependency_coverage.name: Real.lattice

dependency_coverage.meaning: In a lattice-ordered additive group, absolute value is max(a, -a); here it is ordinary real absolute value.

dependency_coverage.name: instHMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructs homogeneous multiplication as an HMul instance from an ordinary Mul instance.

binders: Local definition mu: the Dirac measure at 0 on the Borel real line.
Local definition X: the constant-zero function from the real line to the real line.
Local definition K3: the real number 1.
Universal binder lam in Real for the nonnegative-parameter exponential-integral bound.
Existential binder lam in Real for a negative-parameter counterexample to that bound.
hypotheses: Within the universal clause, lam is assumed to satisfy 0 <= lam.
Within the universal clause, lam is assumed to satisfy lam <= K3^{-1}.
The existential witness is required to satisfy lam < 0 and |lam| <= K3^{-1}.
conclusions: The fixed measure mu is a probability measure.
The fixed function X is measurable.
The fixed scale K3 is positive.
For every real lam with 0 <= lam <= K3^{-1}, the integral with respect to mu of exp(lam * |X(x)|) is at most exp(K3 * lam).
There exists a real lam with lam < 0 and |lam| <= K3^{-1} for which the preceding integral is not at most exp(K3 * lam).
mathematical_definitions: Here mu = delta_0, X(x) = 0 for every real x, and K3 = 1, so K3^{-1} = 1.
The integral is the real-valued measure-theoretic integral over the Borel real line with respect to delta_0.
Absolute value and exponential are the standard real functions.
For these fixed objects the integrand exp(lam * |X(x)|) is identically 1, hence its integral against delta_0 is 1.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Let mu be the unit point mass at 0 on the real line, let X be the identically zero real-valued function, and let K3 = 1. The proposition asserts jointly that mu is a probability measure, X is measurable, and K3 is positive; that for every real parameter lam between 0 and 1, integral exp(lam |X|) dmu <= exp(lam); and that there is nevertheless some real lam between -1 and 0 (strictly negative, with |lam| <= 1) for which this inequality fails. Since the integral is 1, the universal clause is 1 <= exp(lam) for nonnegative lam, while any allowed strictly negative lam supplies 1 > exp(lam) for the final clause.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition concerns only one concrete probability space: the Borel real line with the Dirac measure at 0.
The function X is fixed to the constant zero function and K3 is fixed to 1; there is no quantification over random variables, measures, spaces, or scales.
The universal exponential-integral bound is imposed only for nonnegative lam in [0, 1], not for all lam with |lam| <= 1.
The existential negative witness is nonvacuous: for example lam = -1 satisfies the stated magnitude condition and makes the left side 1 while the right side is exp(-1) < 1.
No explicit integrability premise is present, but for the fixed zero function the integrand is the integrable constant 1 under the finite Dirac probability measure.
The measure, measurability, and positivity facts are conclusions in a concrete conjunction rather than assumptions of a general implication.
